source.author: lucan
source.text: Bacchatur demens aliena per antrum Colla ferens, vittasque dei Phoebeaque serta Erectis discussa comis, per inania templi Ancipiti cervice rotat, spargitque vaganti Obstantes tripodas, magnoque exaestuat igne, Iratum te, Phoebe, ferens.
source.text_original: Bacchatur demens aliena per antrum / Colla ferens, vittasque dei Phoebeaque serta / Erectis discussa comis, per inania templi / Ancipiti cervice rotat, spargitque vaganti / Obstantes tripodas, magnoque exaestuat igne, / Iratum te, Phoebe, ferens.
source.text_english: Madly she raves through the foreign cave, bearing her neck, with the god’s fillets and Phoebus’ garlands shaken from her hair that stands erect; through the voids of the temple she whirls her head this way and that, and scatters the tripods that block her path as she wanders, and boils over with great fire, bearing you in wrath, Phoebus.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_original: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis / ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, / ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus / immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras / surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_english: As the fire, struggling amid the crowded entrails, brought forth the hair and climbed over the quivering innards of the bull, behold, the sacred Mopsus, wholly possessed by the god, terrible to see, was moving along the shore, his fillet and hair rising through the air, and he was brandishing laurel branches.
